independent_failed_prepare_terminal_prob.method: Compile the exact freeze tool bytes in an isolated standard-library process, redirect PREPARE_OUTPUT to a disposable directory, preserve the exact verify_unreviewed_core implementation, and supply an otherwise valid synthetic core alongside both success and failure receipts.

independent_failed_authorization_termina.method: Compile the exact gate bytes in an isolated standard-library process, redirect all authorization paths to a disposable directory, stub unrelated valid document reconstruction inputs, and exercise the exact require_launch_authorization terminal-receipt predicate with coexisting success and failure receipts.

independent_runtime_temp_inode_probe.method: Invoke only atomic_save_runtime_receipt on a disposable output directory and replace the fixed temporary directory entry after its descriptor is closed but before os.replace.

independent_capability_output_binding_pr.method: Invoke only consume_worker_capability on a disposable execution directory with a valid inherited token, secret and PID bindings but a deliberately wrong capability-record output_root.

critical_findings.title: A failed prepare bundle can advance into attach
critical_findings.finding: The post-claim failure handler can publish a fixed prepare directory containing manifest_core.json, a pre-existing success-looking receipt.json and failure_receipt.json. This can occur when writing or syncing the success receipt raises after the directory entry and valid bytes exist. build_attachment and verify_unreviewed_core inspect only manifest_core.json and never require the prepare directory to contain exactly two regular success files, validate the prepare receipt, or reject failure_receipt.json. The failed fixed attempt can therefore become the core for attach.
critical_findings.independent_evidence: Under both Python 3.13.0 and 3.12.14, the exact verify_unreviewed_core implementation accepted a disposable failed prepare bundle containing manifest_core.json, receipt.json and failure_receipt.json.
critical_findings.impact: A terminal failure no longer consumes and closes the prepare stage as the protocol promises. Later reviews and attach can authorize a core originating from an invocation whose terminal state is explicitly failed.
critical_findings.required_fix: Add a same-snapshot successful-prepare verifier before any core review or attach: require freeze_attempt_01 to be a real directory with exactly manifest_core.json and receipt.json as regular read-only files; reconstruct and validate the receipt status, mode, core path, core-file SHA, canonical core SHA, tool/protocol identities, zero-execution fields and completion state; reject every failure receipt, staging entry or extra entry. Bind the successful prepare-receipt SHA into later reviews and attachment. Add dual-interpreter failed/partial/coexisting-receipt negative tests.

critical_findings.title: The canonical gate accepts an authorization lease that also records terminal failure
critical_findings.finding: After authorization and success_receipt.json are published, any catchable exception through the end of main, including a BrokenPipeError from the success print, writes failure_receipt.json. require_launch_authorization reads only success_receipt.json. It never opens the attempt directory with O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW, checks its inode, requires an exact success-only entry set, or rejects failure_receipt.json and authorization.staging.json. A lease can therefore be simultaneously successful and failed while the metadata and full gates return PASS.
critical_findings.independent_evidence: Under both Python 3.13.0 and 3.12.14, the exact require_launch_authorization terminal predicate accepted a disposable attempt directory containing both a valid success_receipt.json and failure_receipt.json.
critical_findings.impact: The gate violates the explicit rule that a failed, partial or merely claimed authorization lease closes launch permanently, so the final authorization state is ambiguous instead of fail closed.
critical_findings.required_fix: Validate the fixed attempt directory itself from a no-follow directory descriptor and require one exact terminal shape: attempt_started.json plus success_receipt.json, with no failure receipt, staging file, symlink or extra entry. Validate both records completely, including manifest SHA, authorization SHA, tool SHA, read-only modes, retry=false, zero generation/pixels and ordered UTC times. Make post-success output reporting occur outside the failure-recording region, or define and enforce one atomic terminal marker. Add dual-interpreter success-plus-failure, success-plus-stage, partial-success and extra-entry negatives.

major_findings.title: The runtime closes the staged receipt descriptor before renaming its pathname
major_findings.finding: atomic_save_runtime_receipt verifies the opened temporary fd, closes it at lines 96-97, and then renames the temporary pathname. It never compares the source pathname inode with the staged fd before or after rename. A replacement in that interval is published over runtime_loading.json; byte comparison detects the corruption only after the prior receipt has already been destroyed.
major_findings.independent_evidence: A disposable deterministic pathname-swap probe caused the exact function to reject only after runtime_loading.json had become SWAPPED_AFTER_FD_CLOSE; the prior FIRST receipt was not preserved.
major_findings.impact: The claimed same-inode publication and failure-evidence preservation do not hold, even though generation fails closed after the post-publication byte check.
major_findings.required_fix: Keep the temporary fd open through publication, capture its device/inode, and require the published destination entry reached through the held directory fd to have that same device/inode before accepting it. Redesign the update sequence so a detected source-entry swap cannot destroy the last valid terminal receipt, and add a deterministic post-open/pre-rename replacement test.

major_findings.title: Capability consumption does not validate the record's output_root
major_findings.finding: The parent writes output_root into worker_capability.json, but consume_worker_capability checks the PIDs, manifest, launcher, execution path, secret and token without checking output_root. The consumption receipt also omits output_root and launcher/execution identities.
major_findings.independent_evidence: The exact consumer accepted a disposable capability record whose output_root was /tmp/UNBOUND_OUTPUT while every checked token, secret, PID, manifest, launcher and execution value was valid.
major_findings.impact: The capability evidence does not establish the protocol's claimed binding to every launch identity. The separate launch ticket still constrains the raw worker's actual output, so this is an evidence-binding defect rather than a demonstrated public worker bypass.
major_findings.required_fix: Carry the expected output root in the inherited capability state or guarded-worker arguments, require the record value to equal the frozen C2 output root, and include output_root, launcher SHA and execution directory in the create-only consumption receipt. Add wrong-output and wrong-parent negative tests.

minor_findings.title: One self-test result label overstates the adversary exercised
minor_findings.finding: The result key capability_wrong_parent_rejected is populated from forged_rejected, but that case supplies an object different from forged_state.token while retaining a matching parent PID. It proves wrong-object rejection, not wrong-parent rejection. The candidate receipt describes it as wrong-object rejection, but the self-test JSON label remains misleading.
minor_findings.required_fix: Rename the result key to capability_wrong_object_rejected and add a separate record/state parent-PID mismatch test.

verified_nonblocking_properties: All eight V4 candidate SHA-256 identities and the assigned self-test receipt SHA matched immediately before this review was written.
The author self-test returned its claimed PASS status under isolated Python 3.13.0 and project Python 3.12.14 without creating any formal C2 path.
The launcher rejects alternate, repeated, equals-form, abbreviated, unknown and public-worker argument vectors and routes the sanitized public namespace only to the guarded parent.
The launcher and runtime full-AST reversible derivations passed under both reviewed interpreters.
Bound source and JSON readers use one O_NOFOLLOW regular-file descriptor snapshot and compile or parse those same bytes; the transitive S39/S35 overrides are active.
The general gate has no caller-controlled unpublished switch; the fixed attachment preflight returns a non-PASS status and the canonical gate requires attachment plus authorization.
The seed-44 YAML is exactly the sealed 879-byte S40 config after its unique seed: 42 to seed: 44 replacement plus one terminal LF, for 880 candidate bytes.
Prepare, attach and authorization use fixed visible or hidden attempt names, and the authorization tool rechecks its attempt-directory inode at two post-claim boundaries.

The monitored parent uses direct fork and a closure-held opaque object plus 256-bit secret; public CLI worker dispatch is absent and single consumption is enforced for all identities actually checked.
The full gate carries a detached manifest snapshot, and runtime receipt publication uses a held output-directory descriptor, O_EXCL, O_NOFOLLOW and post-publication byte validation.
